mainTopic: The end of the טבל wine debate, and the מחלוקת between רבי אליעזר and the חכמים about עירובי תחומין when יום טוב is next to שבת: one holiness or two?
overview: This amud finishes one discussion and starts another. First, the חכמים ask רבי מאיר what happens if the wine flask bursts before תרומה is separated, and he answers that he will deal with it if it happens. Then a new משנה begins about עירובי תחומין when יום טוב falls right next to שבת. רבי אליעזר says each day may have its own עירוב, even in opposite directions, or an עירוב for only one day. The חכמים say it must be one direction for both days, or no עירוב at all, and the משנה explains how one עירוב can serve both nights. The גמרא shows that the debate turns on one question: are the two days one holiness or two? Each side points to rulings the other side accepts. The חכמים answer that they are unsure, so they are strict both ways, and רבי אליעזר answers that the ban on making an עירוב on יום טוב for שבת comes from הכנה. Finally, a ברייתא brings רבי's ruling that each day needs its own working עירוב, and רבי יהודה's opposing view begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The חכמים challenge רבי מאיר: what if the flask bursts?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים challenge רבי מאיר's ruling that a person may drink untithed wine right away, relying on a תרומה separation he plans to make later.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't you at least agree that maybe the flask will burst, and it will turn out that he was drinking טבל all along?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים are attacking רבי מאיר's lenient ruling with a practical danger: the wine he planned to separate as תרומה might be lost.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר lets a person drink now and treat the portion he will separate later as if it were already separated. The חכמים point out that if the flask bursts first, nothing was ever separated. That would mean everything he drank was טבל, looking back.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce from which the required gifts have not yet been separated; forbidden to eat

phrases.english: Don't you concede
that perhaps the flask will burst,
phrases.notes: The wine set aside to be separated later would be lost.

phrases.english: and it will turn out he was drinking tevel retroactively?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אַתָּה מוֹדֶה שֶׁמָּא יִבָּקַע הַנּוֹד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier debate about רבי מאיר's ruling on wine bought from כותים (the previous section is outside this passage).
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's permission to drink right away, relying on a later separation
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The later separation might never happen, so the drinking could turn out to have been eating טבל.

steps.title: רבי מאיר answers: we will deal with it when it bursts
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר rejects the worry and says there is no need to worry about an unlikely accident ahead of time.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: When it bursts, then we will deal with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר answers the challenge by dismissing it. A possible future accident is not a reason to forbid drinking now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר does not deny that the flask could burst. He holds that we follow the normal expectation that it stays whole, and we do not forbid things now because of a rare 'what if.' This closes the earlier סוגיא before the new משנה begins.

keyTerms.meaning: When it bursts (then we will deal with it)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר does not let an unlikely future accident forbid something now. The case is handled only if the accident actually happens.

phrases.english: He said to them: When it bursts.
phrases.notes: Meaning: I will address that if and when it happens.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Dismisses the concern as not relevant right now
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The possibility of the flask bursting should forbid drinking now.
steps.terutzMaskana: We do not worry about an unlikely accident ahead of time. If it happens, it will be handled then.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: two separate עירובין for יום טוב next to שבת
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. רבי אליעזר rules that when יום טוב is next to שבת, a person may set up a different עירוב for each day, even in opposite directions.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי אליעזר says: When יום טוב is next to שבת, whether before it or after it, a person may make two עירובין and say: 'My עירוב on the first day is to the east, and on the second day to the west,' or 'On the first day to the west, and on the second day to the east.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. רבי אליעזר says that two days in a row (יום טוב and שבת) can each get their own עירוב תחומין, pointing in different directions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עירוב תחומין moves a person's 'home base' for the day, so he can walk 2,000 אמות from there. רבי אליעזר treats יום טוב and שבת as two separate days, each with its own holiness, so each day can have its own home base. The גמרא will explain this reasoning later.

keyTerms.meaning: A יום טוב directly next to שבת (Friday or Sunday)
Here: עירובי תחומין, food placed to set a new base for walking limits

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Rabbi Eliezer says:
A Festival adjacent to Shabbat,
whether before it or after it —
phrases.notes: Friday יום טוב or Sunday יום טוב.

phrases.english: a person may establish two eiruvin,
and say: My eiruv on the first day is to the east
and on the second to the west;
on the first to the west and on the second to the east;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic. A new משנה begins after the previous discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, יום טוב and the שבת next to it may each have a separate עירוב, even in opposite directions.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: an עירוב for one day only
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר continues. A person may also make an עירוב for just one of the two days and be like an ordinary townsperson on the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or he may say: 'My עירוב is for the first day, and on the second day I am like the people of my town,' or 'My עירוב is for the second day, and on the first day I am like the people of my town.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר adds another option: use the עירוב on only one day, and on the other day keep the normal limits measured from town.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows from the same idea as step 3. If the two days are fully separate, a person can choose to change his base on one day and leave it unchanged on the other. 'Like the people of my town' means his 2,000 אמות are measured from his home town, as usual.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the people of my town, with normal walking limits measured from town
On the first day / on the second day

phrases.english: My eiruv is for the first day, and on the second I am like the people of my town;
My eiruv is for the second day, and on the first I am like the people of my town.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more options under the same ruling of רבי אליעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, a person may use an עירוב on one day only and keep his town's limits on the other.

steps.title: The חכמים: one direction for both days, or nothing
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים disagree. The two days must share the same עירוב: one direction for both, and both days or neither.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: Either he makes an עירוב in one direction, or he makes no עירוב at all. Either he makes an עירוב for both days, or he makes no עירוב at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים disagree with רבי אליעזר. They do not allow splitting the two days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים reject both of רבי אליעזר's options. 'One direction' rejects the east/west split from step 3. 'Both days' rejects the one-day option from step 4. For them, the two days act as one unit for עירוב purposes. The גמרא will later explore why.
steps.confusionAlert: The two phrases of the חכמים look like they answer רבי אליעזר's two options separately. But the גמרא (step 11) points out that, as written, both phrases come out meaning the same thing: one direction for both days. It then explains that the second phrase is really the חכמים's argument to רבי אליעזר (steps 12–13).
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the core מחלוקת of the משנה. It sets up the גמרא's coming discussion about whether יום טוב and שבת have one holiness or two.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
either he establishes an eiruv in one direction,
or he establishes no eiruv at all.
Either he establishes an eiruv for both days,
or he establishes no eiruv at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי אליעזר's two options.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two days must share one עירוב: same direction, and for both days or for neither.

steps.title: How is a single עירוב used for both days?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks how a person actually makes one עירוב work for both days.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The משנה asks a practical question and answers it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עירוב must exist at nightfall at the start of each day. With two days in a row, there is a practical problem: how does the same food serve both nights? This question introduces the method.

phrases.english: What should one do?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets up the practical method for making one עירוב last for two days.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical way to keep one עירוב valid for two days in a row.

steps.title: The method: bring it, wait for nightfall, take it home, repeat
steps.stepSummary: He brings the עירוב to the place before the first night, waits there until dark, and takes it home. Before the second night he does the same, and then he may eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He brings it there on the first day, stays with it until dark, then takes it and goes home. On the second day he stays with it until dark, then eats it and goes home.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers the question by giving step-by-step instructions for using one עירוב on two nights.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the first night, once it gets dark the עירוב has done its job for that day. He takes it home so it won't be lost before the second night, when it is needed again. After dark on the second night, the עירוב has done its job for that day too, so he may eat it.

keyTerms.meaning: He brings it (to the chosen spot)
He waits with it until nightfall

steps.confusionAlert: Taking the עירוב home after the first night does not cancel it. The עירוב only needs to be in place at nightfall. He takes it so it will be available for the second night.

phrases.english: He brings it on the first day and stays with it until nightfall,
and he takes it, and goes away.
phrases.notes: So it won't be lost before the second night.

phrases.english: On the second day he stays with it until nightfall
and eats it and goes away,

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He brings the עירוב before each night, waits until dark, takes it home after the first night, and may eat it after the second.

steps.title: The double benefit: walking and eating
steps.stepSummary: The משנה sums up: with this method he gains both the right to walk in his chosen direction and the right to eat the עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: So he gains in his walking, and he gains in his עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes by stating the result: the method gives the person two benefits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He gains in walking because his base is moved for both days. He gains in his עירוב because the food is not wasted; he eats it after the second night. The method keeps the עירוב available without losing the food.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר allows a different עירוב for each day. The חכמים require one עירוב for both days. The משנה shows how one עירוב serves both nights: bring it, wait until dark, take it home, repeat, then eat it.

phrases.english: Consequently, he benefits in his walking,
and he benefits in his eiruv.
phrases.notes: He gets to eat it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Summarizes the result of the method in step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: With this method, one עירוב serves both days, and he may still eat the food in the end.

steps.title: If the עירוב was eaten on the first day
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds a case. If the עירוב was eaten on the first day, it works for the first day but not for the second.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it was eaten on the first day, his עירוב works for the first day, and his עירוב does not work for the second day.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the חכמים's method by telling us what happens if the food was already eaten on day one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עירוב only takes effect if the food is there at dusk when the day begins. On the first night the food was there, so day one is covered. If it was eaten during day one, nothing is there at dusk of the second night, so day two gets no עירוב.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the עירוב was 'bad' from the start. It was fully valid for day one. It simply was not there when day two began.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling is exactly what רבי אליעזר uses in the next step to argue against the חכמים.

phrases.english: If it was eaten on the first day
his eiruv is valid for the first day
and his eiruv is not valid for the second day
phrases.notes: The food was not there at dusk of the second night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a case to the method in Steps 7-8: what happens if the עירוב is eaten after day one began.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עירוב eaten on day one covers day one only, not day two.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: you agree they are two separate holinesses
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר tells the חכמים that their own ruling shows the two days are two separate holinesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said to them: You agree with me that they are two separate holinesses.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר uses the חכמים's own ruling from Step 9 as a challenge against them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שבת and יום טוב were one long holiness, an עירוב that took effect on the first night would last for both days, even if it was eaten. Since the חכמים say it does not last, they are treating each day on its own. That is רבי אליעזר's view, so he says each day should also be allowed its own עירוב in its own direction.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who allows a separate עירוב for each day

steps.whyThisMatters: The whole מחלוקת depends on whether the two days are one holiness or two.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said to them:
You agree with me
that they are two separate holinesses.
phrases.notes: So each day should be able to have its own עירוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the חכמים's ruling in Step 9 into an argument against their position in Step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים's rule (Step 5) that both days must share one עירוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Their own ruling that an eaten עירוב does not cover day two treats the days as separate. If the days are separate, separate עירובין should be allowed.

steps.title: The גמרא asks why the Sages' words repeat themselves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the חכמים's two phrases, 'one direction' and 'two days', seem to say the same thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What does 'in one direction' mean? For both days. What does 'for both days' mean? In one direction. That is the same as the first phrase!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks about the wording of the חכמים in the משנה. Their two phrases seem to say the same thing twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים said the עירוב must be 'in one direction' and 'for both days'. Each phrase, once explained, means the same rule: one direction for both days. A משנה is not supposed to repeat itself for no reason, so the גמרא asks what the second phrase adds.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion of the משנה
That is the same as the first one

phrases.english: GEMARA
'In one direction', what does it mean?
For both days.
'For both days', what does it mean?
In one direction.
That is the same as the first one!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The משנה has ended. The גמרא now goes back to the wording of the חכמים in Step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of the חכמים in the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both phrases mean 'one direction for both days', so one of them seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The phrase is really a question the חכמים put to רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the extra phrase is the start of an argument. The חכמים asked רבי אליעזר whether one day can be split between north and south, and he agreed it cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the חכמים were saying to רבי אליעזר: Don't you agree that you cannot make an עירוב for one day with half the day to the north and half to the south? He said to them: Yes, I agree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The second phrase is not a repeated ruling. It is the opening of a debate. The חכמים first get רבי אליעזר to agree on a simple point, which sets up their argument in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים start from something everyone accepts: a single day cannot have half its עירוב in one direction and half in the opposite direction. רבי אליעזר answers 'אבל', meaning 'yes, I agree'. With that agreement in hand, they can now compare it to the two-day case.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what they were saying
Half (the day) to the north and half to the south

steps.confusionAlert: Here אֲבָל does NOT mean 'but'. In this line it means 'Yes, indeed, I agree'.

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי קָאָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר:
phrases.english: This is what the Rabbis were saying to Rabbi Eliezer:
Don't you agree
that one may not make an eiruv for one day
half of it to the north and half of it to the south?
He said to them: Yes, indeed.
phrases.notes: רבי אליעזר agrees on the one-day case.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question in Step 11 by reading the phrase as the חכמים's argument, not a repeated ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the wording: the phrase is part of a debate, not a second ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two phrases are two rulings that say the same thing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The second phrase is the חכמים's argument to רבי אליעזר, starting from a point he accepts.

steps.title: Just as one day cannot be split, two days in a row cannot be split
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים compare the cases. Just as one day cannot be split between two directions, two days of holiness in a row cannot be split between east and west.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as you cannot make an עירוב for one day with half to the south and half to the north, so too you cannot make an עירוב for two days with one day to the east and one day to the west.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים complete their argument. They take the point רבי אליעזר agreed to and apply it to the two-day case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two days of holiness in a row are compared to one single day. Since a single day cannot be split between two directions, the two days cannot each get their own direction either. This explains the extra phrase in the משנה and gives the reason behind the חכמים's position.
steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים treat שבת and יום טוב in a row like one long day when it comes to direction: one עירוב, one direction. רבי אליעזר treats them as two separate holinesses, so each day may have its own עירוב.

phrases.english: Just as one may not make an eiruv for one day
half to the south and half to the north
so too one may not make an eiruv for two days

phrases.aramaic: יוֹם אֶחָד לַמִּזְרָח וְיוֹם אֶחָד לַמַּעֲרָב.
phrases.english: one day to the east and one day to the west.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the point רבי אליעזר agreed to in Step 12 as the basis for comparing the cases.
steps.raayaObject: The חכמים's rule that two days in a row cannot have two different directions.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The agreed rule that one day cannot be split between two directions.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר rejects the comparison: one day versus two days
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers the חכמים' comparison. A single day cannot be split because it is one holiness. Two days in a row are two holinesses, so each day can have its own direction.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what does רבי אליעזר say to this? There, with one day, it is one holiness. Here, with two days, it is two holinesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי אליעזר responds to the חכמים' comparison, and answers that he sees the two cases as different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים argued that two days cannot be split, just like one day cannot be split. רבי אליעזר agrees that one day is one unit of holiness and cannot be divided. But שבת and יום טוב are two separate holinesses, so giving each day a different עירוב is not 'splitting' anything.

keyTerms.meaning: There (the case of one day split north and south)
Here (the case of two days in a row)
One holiness, meaning one single holy unit

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer? (How does he respond?)
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking how רבי אליעזר answers the comparison from Step 13.

phrases.english: There, it is one holiness.
phrases.notes: A single day cannot be split between north and south.

phrases.english: Here, it is two holinesses.
phrases.notes: Two days in a row are separate, so each can have its own עירוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison the חכמים made in Step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between one day and two days
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: One day is one holiness, but two days are two holinesses, so the cases are not alike.
steps.whyThisMatters: The whole debate comes down to this one question: are שבת and יום טוב one holiness or two?

steps.title: רבי אליעזר proves the days are separate from the חכמים' own rulings
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר gets the חכמים to agree to two rulings. You must make a new עירוב with your feet for the second day, and an עירוב eaten on the first day does not work for the second. He concludes that the two days must be two holinesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said to them: Don't you agree that if a person made an עירוב with his feet on the first day, he must make another one with his feet for the second day? And that if his עירוב was eaten on the first day, he cannot use it to go out on the second day? They said to him: Yes. He said: So they are two holinesses!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר uses rulings the חכמים already accept to prove his own view, that the two days are separate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the two days were one holiness, one עירוב should cover both days. But the חכמים require a fresh עירוב for the second day, and they say an עירוב eaten on day one does not help on day two. That treatment only makes sense if each day stands alone, which is exactly רבי אליעזר's claim.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't you agree? (asking someone to admit a point)
Made an עירוב with his feet, by going to the spot and being there at nightfall instead of leaving food there
Isn't it so that...? (concluding from an admission)

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said to them:
Don't you agree
that if he made an eruv with his feet on the first day,
phrases.notes: He physically stood at the spot at nightfall.

phrases.english: he must make an eruv with his feet again for the second day?
If his eruv was eaten on the first day,
he cannot go out by it on the second day.
They said to him: Yes.
phrases.notes: The חכמים admit both rulings.

phrases.english: Then isn't it so that they are two holinesses?
phrases.notes: רבי אליעזר draws his conclusion from their admission.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Step 14 by proving 'two holinesses' from the חכמים' own rulings.
steps.raayaObject: That שבת and יום טוב are two separate holinesses
steps.raayaSupportSource: The חכמים' rulings that each day needs its own עירוב with the feet, and that an עירוב eaten on day one does not work for day two

steps.title: The חכמים are unsure, so they are strict both ways
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains how the חכמים answer. They are not sure whether the two days are one holiness or two, so in every case they take the stricter side.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים? They are in doubt about it. So here they are strict, and here they are strict.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the חכמים by explaining that they never claimed the days are one holiness. They are simply unsure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because of the doubt, the חכמים do not allow two different directions, in case the days are one holiness. They also require a separate עירוב for each day, in case the days are two holinesses. This is not a contradiction. It is being careful both ways.

keyTerms.meaning: They are in doubt about it
To be strict, taking the stricter side

steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים are not changing their minds back and forth. They hold one position, 'we don't know,' and that single doubt makes them strict in both directions.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis? They are in doubt about it,
so here they are strict,
phrases.notes: They do not allow two directions, in case it is one holiness.

phrases.english: and here they are strict.
phrases.notes: They require a new עירוב each day, in case it is two holinesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אליעזר's proof in Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The חכמים are in doubt, so they are strict on both sides
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים' rulings seemed to admit that the days are two holinesses.
steps.terutzMaskana: Their rulings come from doubt, not from agreeing the days are separate, so they are strict either way.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common Talmudic pattern: when a question is in doubt, a ruling can be strict in two directions at once without contradicting itself.

steps.title: The חכמים counter: no making an עירוב on יום טוב for שבת
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים get רבי אליעזר to admit that you cannot first make an עירוב on יום טוב for שבת. They argue this shows the two days are one holiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to רבי אליעזר: Don't you agree that you may not first make an עירוב on יום טוב for שבת? He said to them: Yes. They said: So it is one holiness!
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים answer back with a ruling that רבי אליעזר himself accepts, to show the days are linked as one holiness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שבת were a completely separate holiness, its עירוב would only need to take effect when שבת begins, so a person could set it up during יום טוב as he would on an ordinary Friday. Yet רבי אליעזר agrees this is not allowed. To the חכמים, this shows the two days form one holiness, whose עירוב must already be in place before the first day begins.

keyTerms.meaning: Making an עירוב for the first time, when none was made beforehand
From יום טוב for שבת, meaning on יום טוב for the שבת that follows

steps.whatToRemember: Each side uses the other's admitted rulings. רבי אליעזר says the days are two holinesses. The חכמים are unsure, so they are strict both ways, and they point to a case that makes the days look like one holiness.

phrases.english: They said to Rabbi Eliezer:
Don't you agree
that one may not make an eruv for the first time
on Yom Tov for Shabbat?
phrases.notes: For example, יום טוב falls on Friday and he forgot to make an עירוב beforehand.

phrases.english: He said to them: Yes.
Then isn't it so that it is one holiness!
phrases.notes: The חכמים draw their conclusion from his admission.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: אִי אַתָּה מוֹדֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The חכמים counter רבי אליעזר's proof with one of their own, built the same way.
steps.raayaObject: That שבת and יום טוב are one holiness
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אליעזר's admission that one may not first make an עירוב on יום טוב for שבת

steps.title: רבי אליעזר says that rule comes from the ban on preparing
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר rejects the חכמים' proof. You cannot make an עירוב on יום טוב for שבת because of הכנה, not because the two days are one holiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר? He says: there, the reason is the ban on preparing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי אליעזר answers the proof the חכמים brought in the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים said: 'You agree you cannot make an עירוב on יום טוב for שבת, so the two days must be one holiness.' רבי אליעזר says that rule has a different reason. Even two separate holinesses have a ban on using one holy day to prepare for the next (הכנה), so his view that they are two holinesses still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: There, in that case (the case of making an עירוב on יום טוב for שבת)
Because of, for the reason of
Preparing on one holy day for a different day, which is not allowed

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר does not deny the rule that you cannot make an עירוב on יום טוב for שבת. He agrees with that rule. He only gives a different reason for it, so the rule no longer proves that the two days are one holiness.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא move. Two sides can agree on the law and still disagree about the reason for it. Once a second reason is offered, the agreed law no longer proves either side.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer (how does he answer?):
phrases.notes: Short גמרא formula meaning 'How would רבי אליעזר respond?'

phrases.english: There, it is because of preparation.
phrases.notes: The ban on making an עירוב on יום טוב for שבת comes from הכנה, not from 'one holiness.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof the חכמים brought in step 17 by giving a different reason for the agreed rule.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. The halacha that you may not make an עירוב on יום טוב for שבת stays in place.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The rule can be explained by the ban on הכנה, so it does not show that the two days are one holiness.

steps.title: A ברייתא: a new עירוב is needed for the second day
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records רבי's ruling. If you made an עירוב with your feet for the first day, you must do it again for the second day. If your food עירוב was eaten on the first day, it does not work for the second day. Then רבי יהודה begins to state a different view.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If someone made an עירוב with his feet on the first day, he must make an עירוב with his feet again on the second day. If his עירוב was eaten on the first day, he cannot rely on it to go out on the second day. These are the words of רבי. רבי יהודה says:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with clear rulings about an עירוב over two holy days in a row. The ברייתא then starts to bring רבי יהודה's different opinion, which continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These two rulings are the same ones the חכמים admitted to רבי אליעזר earlier in the argument (step 15). Here they appear in the name of רבי, who treats each day strictly: each day needs its own working עירוב. The words 'רבי יהודה אומר' show that another תנא disagrees, and his view will come next.

keyTerms.meaning: He made an עירוב with his feet, by going to the spot and being there at nightfall
His עירוב (the food he put down) was eaten
He cannot go out (past the normal limit) by relying on it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'רבי' and 'רבי יהודה.' Plain 'רבי' is רבי יהודה הנשיא. 'רבי יהודה' is a different, earlier תנא, and he is about to disagree.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי, each of the two days needs its own working עירוב. Walking there for day one, or food that was eaten on day one, does not take care of day two.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
phrases.notes: Opens a ברייתא.

phrases.english: If he made an eruv with his feet on the first day,
phrases.notes: He walked to the spot before the first day began and was there at nightfall.

phrases.english: he must make an eruv with his feet on the second day.
phrases.notes: He has to go to the spot again before the second day begins.

phrases.english: If his eruv was eaten on the first day,
phrases.notes: This is a food עירוב, not one made with feet.

phrases.english: he may not go out relying on it on the second day,
phrases.notes: He cannot walk past the town's limit by relying on that עירוב.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi (Yehuda HaNasi).
phrases.notes: Plain 'רבי' means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
phrases.notes: Opens a different opinion. His words continue on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: עֵירַב בְּרַגְלָיו בְּיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the רבי אליעזר and חכמים argument ends, the גמרא brings a ברייתא that states the same עירוב rulings in the name of רבי, with רבי יהודה about to disagree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי: an עירוב made with the feet must be made again for the second day, and a food עירוב eaten on the first day does not work for the second day.
